identity.name: ENGINEERS INDIA LTD
identity.industry: Engineering & Consulting for Oil & Gas, Hydrogen & Petrochemical Infrastructure

summary.oneLiner: EIL delivered strong Q2FY26 performance with 50% PBT growth and record order book of ₹13,131cr, driven by international consultancy wins and margin expansion; the key shift is sustained 25%+ consultancy margin despite LSTK revenue mix, and near-term catalysts are accelerating in hydrogen and overseas markets.

one-line thesis: EIL delivered strong Q2FY26 performance with 50% PBT growth and record order book of ₹13,131cr, driven by international consultancy wins and margin expansion; the key shift is sustained 25%+ consultancy margin despite LSTK revenue mix, and near-term catalysts are accelerating in hydrogen and overseas markets.
financial scorecard: revenue: ₹900cr (+33% YoY); EBITDA/margin: ₹160cr / 17% (+45% YoY / +200bps); PAT (rptd): ₹115cr (+45% YoY); PAT (normalized): ₹80cr (ex-₹35cr provision reversal); order book: ₹13,131cr (all-time high, +8% QoQ); net debt: net cash position (₹900-1000cr cash on balance sheet)
guidance: revenue growth: 25%+ YoY; margin: consultancy 25%, LSTK 6-7%; order inflow: >₹8,000cr (already ₹4,000cr in H1); capex/commissioning: minimal capex; focus on commissioning of Ramagundam plant (Q3FY26)
order book & pipeline: ₹13,131cr as of 30-Sep-2025; H1FY26 order inflow: ₹3,765cr; total order pipeline >₹4,000cr (beyond H1); international orders: ₹1,600cr in H1; domestic orders: ₹2,400cr in H1
segment / subsidiary detail: Consultancy: ₹411cr (46% of revenue), 28% segment margin; LSTK: ₹489cr (54% of revenue), 6-7% segment margin; international consultancy: ₹75cr Q2 (down from ₹100cr due to Dangote wind-down, but pipeline strong); domestic consultancy: ₹336cr Q2
growth verticals / optionality: Hydrogen projects (NTPC coal-to-SNG award); bio-refinery (bamboo-based); coal gasification; international expansion in MENA (Abu Dhabi, Africa); Andhra BPCL refinery & petchem studies; IOCL Paradip Phase-2 (expected end-FY26); AGCPL petchem expansion
margins & cost dynamics: Consultancy margin: 28% Q2 (25% H1), sustained at 25%+ guidance; LSTK margin: 6-7%; no material cost inflation impact; provision reversals (₹35cr Q2) are routine and not structural; pay commission impact already factored in
capex / expansion: Minimal capex; company is net cash positive (₹900-1000cr); no major capex planned; capital allocation focused on strategic equity investments (NRL, RFCL) and potential bolt-on acquisitions
capital allocation: Cash balance: ₹900-1000cr; deployed per DPE guidelines; focus on low-capex, high-return opportunities like NRL and RFCL; no dividend policy announced; equity investments held for strategic exposure, not yield; no buybacks or special dividends mentioned
risks & watch-items: Ramagundam plant operational stability (past shutdowns); delay in IOCL Paradip Phase-2 award; tariff disputes stalling private petchem projects; international execution delays; currency volatility on overseas projects; provision reversals are volatile but not material to core earnings
management quality / tone: Confident and bullish; emphasized record order book, margin discipline, and international growth; reiterated guidance; downplayed one-offs (provision reversals); expressed strong pipeline in hydrogen and MENA; tone is execution-focused and optimistic
non-obvious takeaways: EIL's ₹13,131cr order book includes ₹4,000cr+ in pipeline beyond H1, implying full-year inflow may exceed ₹8,000cr; consultancy revenue lags order wins due to project ramp-up (Dangote wind-down masked growth); Ramagundam's ₹491cr investment could yield ₹130cr annual PAT (26% stake) once stabilized; EIL is effectively a 'project incubator' for India's energy transition with zero capex risk
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ramagundam plant shutdowns dragging consolidated PAT | Engineers India Limited | beneficiary | High | Q3FY26 profitability return from RFCL could add ₹100cr+ to consolidated PAT, removing a major earnings overhang |
| Dangote refinery revenue wind-down masking international consultancy growth | Engineers India Limited | beneficiary | High | New international orders (₹1,600cr H1) will ramp up in H2FY26, driving consultancy revenue recovery |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
